Everything is healthy, and I made no scheduling change this run (05:35).

**Running work**
- **FEBio:** 10 runs going (9 physrotFr3, 1 pilotTie3_p053) and 61 physrotFr3 waiting, the oldest queued at 04:04. All 10 logs updated within the last 25 s. 2278 done, 2 failed. Only 1 run finished in the last 3 h: pilotTie_p023, which was already reported.
- **Task queue (new repo):** 0 waiting, 0 running, 1 done, 5 failed (the same 5 since 10-28).
- **Services:** all 6 tmux services are up. The NAS archive script is copying `cases` (364 GB, started 04:32); its restart entry in `ops/resume_all.sh` correctly stays inactive while it runs.

**Resources**
- **CPU:** this is the only thing limiting speed. We use 29.4–31.2 of our 32-core quota; the whole machine is at load 73 of 256.
- **Memory:** 57 GB used by programs out of 137 GB. The rest is file cache from the NAS copy, which the system can free. No out-of-memory kills.
- **GPUs:** all 7 are used by other users (weimin2, thlin, linjimmy1003), none by us. FEBio runs on CPU only, so that costs nothing.
- **Disk:** 2.2 TB free on /raid.

**Decision: kept 10 runs at once (`CPU_OVERCOMMIT` 1.25)**
- The last run said to go back to 9 if the CPU quota throttled more than 40% of the time. It is now throttled 55–64% of the time.
- But each run still gets the same CPU: about 2.97 cores with 9 runs, 2.94–3.12 with 10. Total CPU use is 10–17% higher. The throttle figure counts time slices, not lost work.
- So I kept 10 and changed the rule: go back to 9 if a run gets less than 2.6 cores.
- An 11th run would need about 33 cores, more than the quota.

**Needs a person**
- pilotTie_p023 stopped with a "negative Jacobian" error (the mesh turned inside out) even though the scheduler log shows success. I did not restart it; this is a science question.
- The NAS archive script checks whether FEBio is using a folder by looking at the command line, but it should look at each process's working directory (`/proc/*/cwd`).
- The 5 failed tasks from 10-28 still need an owner; T01, T16, T10 and the al_loop gate are still undecided.
- The 61 waiting runs will take about 45–55 h. Only a bigger CPU quota would make that faster.
